prerequisites: Knowledge of the basics of thermofluid sciences (thermodynamics, heat transfer and fluid flow).
Knowledge of the fundamentals of numerical methods.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic principles and structure of CFD simulation systems.
Understand discretisation problems: consistency, stability, convergence, discretisation order, numerical diffusion etc.
To be aware of the peculiarities when solving the fluid flow equations and the problems regarding numerical modelling of turbulent flow.
To be able to choose the appropriate formulation and numerical approach for the given physical problem and to assess the correctness of the obtained results.
To be equipped with the practical skill of solving a spectrum of problems by a CFD simulation system.

syllabus_topics: Overview of the governing equations describing different types of fluid flow.
Essential elements and historical developments of CFD.
Space and time discretisation of transport phenomena fields.
Elaboration of the finite volume method for CFD.
Industrial CFD examples from the fields of materials processing, aerodynamics, biomedicine, environmental sciences etc.

assessment_methods.method: Theory - from lectures and exercise problems
Project with a CFD code (ANSYS FLUENT and/or OpenFOAM)

bibliography: F. Moukalled, L. Mangani, M. Darwish, The Finite Volume Method in Computational Fluid Dynamics: An Advanced Introduction with OpenFOAM and Matlab, Springer Verlag, Cham, 2016.
H. K. Versteeg, W. Malalasekera, An Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics, The Finite Volume Method, 2nd Edition, Pearson, Harlow, 2007.
G.R. Liu, Mesh Free Methods: Moving Beyond Finite Element Method, CRC Press, Boca Raton, 2nd Edition, 2009.
degree: Mechanical Engineering (2nd cycle, Erasmus+ subjects, Research and Development programme)
